text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- CURRENT ACCT GAP WORRISOME BUT GOV'T SEES OPTIONS

Former Central Bank chief Affonso Celso Pastore said Brazil remains hostage to a tight monetary policy due to its fragile external accounts, including a projected $35 billion current account gap this year. But Finance Ministry Economic Policy Secretary Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros expects foreign accounts to improve as exports grow this year.
-- KANDIR EXPECTS TO RAISE 25 BLN REAIS VIA PRIVATIZATIONS
The Brazilian government expects to raise 25 billion reais through privatizations in 1997 and 1998, said Planning Minister Antonio Kandir.
-- UNIBANCO LEASING RAISES 1.0 BLN REAIS
Unibanco Leasing Arrendamento Mercantil, a unit of private bank Unibanco, issued one billion reais in six-year debentures.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- GOV'T MOVES TO AVOID BROAD PROBE ON VOTE-BUYING SCHEME
Government leaders in the Chamber of Deputies are making an effort to prevent lawmakers from setting up a broad congressional inquiry into an alleged cash-for-votes scam involving a re-election bill.
-- TRANSPORTS MAY STOP TOMORROW IN SAO PAULO
Sao Paulo bus and subway workers may go on strike Wednesday to demand higher salaries.
O GLOBO
-- GOVERNMENT ALLOWS LIFTING OF BANK SECRECY

Finance Minister Pedro Malan issued a ministerial decree lifting bank secrecy in order for banks to provide government information on their clients's monthly banking transactions to ensure collection of CPMF taxes.
-- TELEPHONE SUBSCRIPTION RATE RISES 270 PCT
The latest round of telephone rate adjustments took effect Monday. Residential subscription rates are now 270.37 percent higher across the country, said Communications Ministry.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
